verification: Figure 1 topology visually inspected from the embedded PDF image

global_goal: For the stated production systems, make inspection, acceptance/rejection, assembly-product inspection, disposal, and disassembly/reuse decisions with explicitly tracked probabilities and economic consequences.

data_inventory.description: A supplier claims a component-batch defect rate does not exceed a nominal value; the required numerical instance is 10%.

Six cases giving component-1/component-2/finished-product defect rates; component purchase and inspection costs; finished-product assembly and inspection costs; selling price; exchange loss; and disassembly cost.
data_inventory.unit: yuan per item except defect rates

data_inventory.description: Assembly DAG: components 1-3 to semi-finished product 1; 4-6 to semi-finished product 2; 7-8 to semi-finished product 3; the three semi-finished products to the finished product.

All eight component defect rates are 10%; component purchase prices are [2,8,12,2,8,12,8,12] and inspection costs [1,1,2,1,1,2,1,2]. Each of three semi-finished products has defect rate 10%, assembly cost 8, inspection cost 4, and disassembly cost 6. The finished product has defect rate 10%, assembly cost 8, inspection cost 6, disassembly cost 10, selling price 200, and exchange loss 40.
data_inventory.unit: yuan per item except defect rates

data_inventory.description: Semi-finished-product and finished-product defect rates are conditional defect rates after assembling qualified inputs; exchange loss excludes the cost of replacing the defective item; all monetary values are yuan/item.

global_constraints: A finished product is certainly defective if either component is defective; even two qualified components can produce a defective finished product.
Disassembly does not damage components but incurs its stated cost.
When an uninspected component is selected, it enters assembly directly; inspected defective components are discarded.
A customer-returned defective product follows the stated disassembly-or-discard decision branch.
Question 1 explicitly requires minimizing the number of inspections while satisfying its confidence statements.

subquestions.statement: Design a sampling-inspection plan with as few inspections as possible for supplier components. With nominal rate 10%, give a plan for rejecting a batch when its defect rate is judged above the nominal value at 95% confidence, and for accepting a batch when it is judged not above the nominal value at 90% confidence.
subquestions.goal: Produce an operational acceptance/rejection sampling rule and its minimal required inspection count under a declared statistical interpretation.
inputs: observed defective count in the sample
constraints: inspection count is an explicit minimization objective
the two stated confidence conditions must be met
detection cost is borne by the enterprise
required_outputs: specific numerical sampling results for the two 10% cases
success_criteria: statistical guarantee is stated without reversing the direction of inference
the rule is executable from observed data
no fixed arbitrary sample size substitutes for the minimization
dependencies: Provides the sampling-based defect-rate input and uncertainty treatment for Q4.
ambiguities: The statement does not specify a producer's/consumer's risk pair, an indifference zone, whether a fixed-sample or sequential plan is intended, or the observed number of defects for the two requested numerical outcomes. These alternatives materially change the meaning of 'minimum inspections'.

subquestions.statement: For each of six Table-1 cases with known rates and costs, decide component inspection, finished-product inspection, and disassembly versus discard for defective products or customer returns; report the plan, its basis, and indicators.
subquestions.goal: Find an economically preferred complete production policy for each Table-1 case.
inputs: Table-1 defect rates and all stated per-item costs
constraints: all probability branches must be accounted for
detected defective inspected components are discarded
disassembly components re-enter the stated inspection/assembly steps
customer replacement and exchange loss apply to an uninspected defective item reaching the market
success_criteria: every cost and reuse/discard branch is counted exactly once
the chosen policy has practical economic meaning
dependencies: Uses the same inspection/disassembly logic generalized in Q3; its known defect rates are replaced by sampled estimates in Q4.
proposed_relationships: Expected cost or expected profit can be evaluated for each admissible policy once the interpretation of the reuse loop is fixed.
ambiguities: The statement says disassembled components repeat steps (1) and (2), but does not explicitly state whether reuse continues indefinitely or is limited by a practical cycle/termination convention. This affects expected-value accounting if a loop is modeled literally.

subquestions.statement: For m processes and n components with known component, semi-finished-product, and finished-product defect rates, repeat Q2. The provided instance has two assembly stages and eight components as specified by Figure 1 and Table 2.
subquestions.goal: Find an economically preferred production policy on a multi-stage assembly DAG.
inputs: Table-2 defect rates, prices, costs and losses
unknowns_or_decisions: inspection decision for every component, semi-finished product and final product
disassembly/discard decision at each defective node
constraints: conditional process defect rates in the appendix
all inspection, assembly, loss, disassembly and reuse branches
required_outputs: concrete policy for the provided instance
a formulation applicable to m processes and n components
success_criteria: state, action, transition and terminal conditions are explicit if a dynamic-programming/decision formulation is used
the Figure-1 strategy space is complete
dependencies: Generalizes Q2; Q4 replaces known rates by sampling-derived uncertain estimates.
proposed_relationships: The provided topology is (1,2,3)->S1, (4,5,6)->S2, (7,8)->S3, and (S1,S2,S3)->final product.
ambiguities: As in Q2, a literal repeated reuse loop requires an explicit termination or infinite-horizon expected-value convention; the requested level of generality for arbitrary m and n must also be declared.

subquestions.statement: Assume the component, semi-finished-product, and finished-product defect rates in Q2 and Q3 are obtained by sampling inspection, for example with the Q1 method; redo Q2 and Q3.
subquestions.goal: Re-evaluate the Q2/Q3 decisions while propagating uncertainty from sampling-derived defect rates.
unknowns_or_decisions: uncertainty representation for each defect rate
decision rule robust to or conditional on that uncertainty
same operational inspection/disassembly decisions as Q2/Q3
constraints: must not treat estimated rates as known without recording sampling uncertainty
must retain all Q2/Q3 cost and transition branches
required_outputs: basis and indicators that reflect sampling uncertainty
success_criteria: the Q1 inferential output connects consistently to the decision model
uncertainty can change or qualify a policy where evidence requires it
dependencies: Depends on Q1 for rate inference and on Q2/Q3 for the production-decision structure.
proposed_relationships: A policy can be evaluated conditionally on estimates, conservatively over confidence sets, or by integrating an explicitly selected uncertainty model; selection requires human judgment.
ambiguities: The statement does not prescribe frequentist versus Bayesian uncertainty propagation, confidence level allocation across many rates, or a risk criterion for deciding under estimated rates.

human_decisions_needed.reason: Before method screening, the workflow requires the modeler to choose the output form, priority, unacceptable failure and experiment budget. Q1 also needs a load-bearing interpretation of minimum inspections.
